title: Responsive navigation transformation
summary: Change the presentation of navigation across breakpoints while preserving information architecture, labels, destination order, and access.
problem: Responsive redesigns often remove or reorder important destinations, making mobile a functionally different product.
use_when: Primary navigation cannot fit comfortably at narrow widths
The same product serves touch and desktop contexts
avoid_when: The navigation already fits and remains comfortably operable
A mobile-specific product has intentionally different information architecture backed by user needs
rationale: Responsive design should adapt presentation before it removes capability.
Stable labels and hierarchy reduce cross-device relearning.

prefer_alternatives_if: The narrow layout can preserve the same navigation visibly without overflow
use_if: Primary navigation cannot fit comfortably at narrow widths
The same product serves touch and desktop contexts

requirements: Menu disclosure must expose expanded/collapsed state.
Do not require hover to reveal destinations.
Ensure touch targets and spacing remain operable.
Preserve destination set unless a documented product decision says otherwise.
Do not hide critical actions inside unrelated menus.
